text: Two views answer different questions. A breakdown view shows smaller parts within a larger whole. An interface view identifies the relationships between those parts and the surrounding world. Inputs, outputs and outside dependencies often reveal integration or operational risks. A diagram guides investigation; it is not evidence that the design has been validated.

items: Choose the system of interest. You should see: A named system. If not: Narrow the boundary until it can be described.
Group its major elements. You should see: A short hierarchy. If not: Keep only useful detail at this stage.
Draw external connections and label their purpose. You should see: Each link has a reason to exist. If not: Ask what information, power, people, or material crosses.
Illustration: Treat the platform as the system of interest and a remote communication service as external. Show the information exchanged at their connection.

text: Use one picture to inventory parts and another to investigate links and boundaries.
A boundary view is incomplete when important outside systems are missing.
